dataset_family: Local senior centres, South Korea (Soonchunhyang University; single author J-H Park; TCTR20220418003); 84 HC / 52 amnestic MCI
method_family: 8-channel prefrontal fNIRS (task-evoked oxy-haemoglobin, mHbO) during a verbal digit span task, compared with MoCA-K by ROC
what_it_shows: Park 2023, Front Aging Neurosci 15:1137283. Task-evoked prefrontal mHbO during the verbal digit span task is lower in amnestic MCI than in healthy controls (left PFC t = 10.100, p < 0.001; AUC 0.952). The MoCA-K also separates the groups strongly (t = 10.595, p < 0.001; AUC 0.902), and so does behavioural performance on the same digit-span task (t = 6.965, p < 0.001). MMSE-K does not differ (26.21 vs 26.02, p = 0.423), but intact MMSE-K global cognition was an inclusion criterion for MCI, and Table 1 reports MMSE-K as a matching characteristic.
why: No. (1) The study's own head-to-head is fNIRS mHbO versus MoCA-K, and both separate MCI from controls. The paper's claim is better discriminant power (AUC 0.952 vs 0.902), which is a diagnostic-accuracy comparison, not a case where the static measure fails. The VF-25 record itself scopes the claim as sensitivity, not accuracy. (2) The unloaded behavioural measure of the same task (VDST score) also separates the groups (p < 0.001), so there is no loaded-versus-unloaded dissociation on the task. (3) The only non-separating static measure is MMSE-K. Its null is produced by the design: 'intact global cognitive function confirmed by the Korean version of mini-mental state examination' was an MCI inclusion criterion, and the Results report it alongside age, sex and education as a matched characteristic. It is not a static measure failing where a loaded one succeeds. (4) The loaded measure is haemodynamic (fNIRS), not one of the statement's named limbs (diffusion microstructure, task-evoked electrophysiology, dual-task performance). Other limits the author states: no cross-validation (overfitting acknowledged), PFC-only coverage, amnestic-only MCI. No shared cohort, site or authors with any current supporter or with the other candidates. Not a preprint.

quotes.quote: According to these studies, the inclusion criteria for MCI were defined as follows: (1) a subjective memory complaint, (2) objective memory impairment confirmed by performances on the neuropsychological battery (Seoul Neuropsychological Screening Battery), (3) intact global cognitive function confirmed by the Korean version of mini-mental state examination, (4) independent activities of daily living, and (5) no dementia diagnosis confirmed by a physician.
No significant difference in age, sex ration, education periods, and global cognition between the healthy group and MCI group was found (Table 1).

The healthy group outperformed the MCI group in both the MoCA-K and the VDST (p's < 0.001), indicating that the healthy group showed a better global cognition and working memory than the MCI group (Table 2). On the other hand, in brain signals, no noisy channel was observed, and there were significant differences between the healthy group and the MCI group in left, right, and total PFC (p's < 0.001; Table 2).
